projects.title: Viar-OS: My Custom Arch Linux Distribution
projects.description: Viar OS is a meticulously crafted Linux distribution, meticulously designed to provide users with a seamless and efficient computing experience.
projects.fullDescription:
🔹 What Makes Viar-OS Special

- 🖥️ Multi-Desktop Support– Choose from multiple desktop environments.  
- 🔄 Rolling Updates – Uses Pacman & Paru for always up-to-date packages.  
- 🛠️ Easy Installation– Online + offline install via Calamares.  
- 📂 BTRFS + Snapshots – Built-in rollback and disaster recovery.  
- ⚡ Zram Compression – Optimizes RAM usage for better performance on low-RAM systems.  
- 🎨 Polished UI/UX – Clean design with practical customization.  
- ❤️ Open Source – Code and configs available for exploration.

🔹 Technical Skills Demonstrated

- Linux Internals – Kernel configuration, package management, system tuning  
- Filesystem Management – BTRFS setup and snapshot handling  
- Automation – Bash & Python scripts for install and system configuration  
- Desktop Configuration – Multi-DE support, theming, UX tweaks  
- Version Control & Docs – GitHub project management and documentation  
- Performance Optimization – Tuned for low-resource systems

Viar-OS helped me develop skills as both a Linux developer and distro maintainer—balancing usability, stability, and performance.

🔗 https://viar-os.github.io

projects.title: Real-World DevOps Project: Kubernetes + ArgoCD on My Home Lab!
projects.description: Just Completed a Real-World DevOps Project: Kubernetes + ArgoCD on My Home Lab!
projects.fullDescription:
Last week, I took my cloud-native skills to the next level by recreating the - but with my own twist!

Instead of AWS EC2, I deployed a full Kubernetes (K3s) cluster inside Proxmox LXC containers on my home server.Why? To show what’s possible even on personal hardware, and to master efficient, scalable deployments accessible to everyone!

🔑 Highlights of the project:

- Automated Application Deployment with ArgoCD: Achieved GitOps-driven, seamless CI/CD pipeline management.
- Fully Visual Management: Leveraged Kubernetes Dashboard for real-time ops and monitoring.
- High Availability & Scaling: Configured for resilient 99.9% uptime—yes, in a home lab!
- Resource Efficiency: Maximized server utilization and cost-savings using lightweight K3s and Proxmox LXC.
- Inspirational Approach: Proved you don’t need expensive cloud VM instances to master modern DevOps—DIY setups are powerful learning experiences for freshers and veterans alike!

Why does this matter?

If you’re a recruiter seeking hands-on, self-driven DevOps engineers, or a DevOps enthusiast wanting to replicate the real-world skills in your own lab—reach out or get inspired!

projects.fullDescription:
One of the projects I've worked on recently was a chance to handle the infrastructure side of an Agentic AI platform. The dev team built a custom agentic application, basically an AI-powered workflow automation platform. My job was to take it from code to a secure, scalable, highly available Kubernetes platform.

🔹 What I did:

- Containerized the application and designed its deployment architecture on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
- Architected the platform for 1,000+ concurrent users with dedicated agent pods, focusing on workload isolation, reliability, and scalability.
- Set up GitOps + Azure DevOps-based workflows to automate and standardize application releases.
- Added Cilium networking with Azure BYO CNI for stronger network control and workload isolation within AKS.
- Integrated Terraform, Trivy, Checkov, and SonarQube to bring Infrastructure-as-Code and security controls into the delivery pipeline.
- Designed HPA and auto-scaling for changing workloads, targeting better than 99.5% availability.
- Added Prometheus and Grafana for infrastructure and application observability.

The part I enjoyed wasn't just figuring out how to deploy the application. It was how to securely run isolated agent workloads for 1,000+ users, scale them when needed, automate the entire delivery lifecycle, and keep everything reliable at the same time. That's the kind of infrastructure and platform engineering I like doing.
